title: hinted-kv-block-cycler-and-lazy-slab-sanitizer
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Under certain mixed workloads we observed tail-latency spikes and increased fragmentation when the paged KV cache accumulated low-utilization slabs that were never reclaimed aggressively. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: 1) a hinted KV block cycler that incrementally promotes eviction on blocks tagged by runtime heuristics, and 2) a lazy slab sanitizer that performs low-cost in-place compaction and inconsistency checks during quiet CPU cycles. The combination reduces fragmentation and amortizes reclamation work without harming p99 latency.

Design & assumptions: The cycler receives lightweight hints from the scheduler and serving runtime (miss counters, inter-request gaps, and occupancy heat markers). Hinted blocks are placed on a prioritized circular queue (cycler ring) where aging promotes eviction eligibility, but they are not forcibly unpinned; instead the allocator will prefer these blocks for reuse when creating new allocations. The lazy slab sanitizer watches for under-utilized slabs (below a configurable occupancy threshold) and performs gentle compaction steps: moving live entries to neighboring blocks where possible, repairing small allocation metadata inconsistencies, and emitting metrics if repairs exceed a tolerance. Sanitizer work is strictly throttled by a CPU budget token so it only runs in less busy windows.

What changed (summary): Implemented cycler ring data structure, hook points in the scheduling pipeline to emit hints, allocator preference logic to consume hinted blocks first, and a background lazy_slab_sanitizer worker with adaptive backoff. Added unit tests for cycler behavior, integration tests simulating mixed read/write workloads, and a small e2e perf harness used in the canary cluster. Updated docs for tuning knobs (cycler.window_ms, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms).

Commits: 
- 3f8b2a1: introduce cycler ring and basic enqueue/dequeue semantics
- 8d9c4f0: wire scheduler hint emission and lightweight telemetry aggregation
- b27f1de: allocator: prefer hinted blocks and add allocation scoreboard
- a4c91e3: lazy_slab_sanitizer worker and compaction primitives
- d1e4ab9: tests + perf harness + docs

Files touched (high-level): 
- runtime/kv/cycler.cc (new) 
- runtime/kv/cycler.h (new) 
- runtime/kv/allocator.cc (modified): consume hinted blocks path, allocation scoreboard
- runtime/kv/sanitizer.cc (new) 
- runtime/scheduler/hints.cc (modified): emit hints based on request patterns
- tests/kv/cycler_test.cc (new)
- tests/kv/sanitizer_integration_test.py (new)
- docs/ops/kv_tuning.md (modified)

Review conversation (high level): 
- Diego Alvarez: "Overall looks good; two main asks: add a safety metric for sanitizer-induced copying and make sure cycler hints cannot starve optimistic reuse paths."
- Maya Chen (author): "Added sanitizer.copy_bytes metric and a sanitizer.max_copy_bytes_per_window config; cycler now sets a soft TTL per-entry to avoid indefinite deprioritization of blocks."
- Priya Nair: "Can you add a deterministic unit test for the ring wrap case and a CI job exercising sanitizer under high concurrency?"
- Maya Chen: "Added cycler_test for wrap and a lightweight high-concurrency integration test; heavy stress runs tracked in attached perf harness (not in CI)."
- Evan Brooks: "Minor: please document knobs in docs/ops/kv_tuning.md and include suggested defaults for Dedicated and Hosted tiers."
- Maya Chen: "Docs updated; defaults: cycler.window_ms=5000, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold=0.22, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms=10 per core."

CI & checks: 
- unit (linux) — pass
- integration (small) — pass
- lint — pass
- perf-canary — initial run flagged a small regression on a synthetic write-heavy workload (p50 unchanged, p99 up ~5%); reran with sanitizer off-by-default in canary and adjusted sanitizer backoff heuristics; final canary run passed.

Benchmarks: 
- Mixed read/write synthetic (50/50 at 8k qps): net reduction in allocator fragmentation metric by ~38%, average memory overhead down ~12MB per node, and CPU cost of sanitizer approx 3% of spare cycles in steady state. Observed 7-12% reduction in allocation latencies in high-churn scenarios.

Migration & ops notes: 
- The sanitizer is off by default in hosted for the first rollout. Operators can enable via runtime flag sanitizer.enabled=true. The cycler is safe to enable by default because it only changes preference heuristics and does not force evictions. Tuning guidance in docs/ops/kv_tuning.md.

Release notes: 
- Introduces hinted KV block cycler to reduce fragmentation under mixed workloads.
- Adds lazy slab sanitizer that performs safe low-cost in-place compaction.
- New tuning knobs: cycler.window_ms, sanitizer.occupancy_threshold, sanitizer.cpu_budget_ms.

Risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: sanitizer could increase p99 if aggressive; mitigation: default off in hosted canary, strict CPU budget and backoff, explicit safety metrics to auto-disable if regressions detected.
- Risk: incorrect hinting could delay reuse of useful blocks; mitigation: soft TTL on hints and fallback to normal allocation after TTL.

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers after two rounds of changes. All CI checks green on final run. Squash-merged into main by Diego Alvarez on 2026-02-24.
